messages.subject: Direction of trait scale
parts:
When I compute binary indicator thresholds using glm they have the opposite sign to thresholds computed by lavaan.
Is the scale direction arbitrary or is there some reason why these signs are opposite?

For example:

tmp = HolzingerSwineford1939[,c("x1","x2","x3","x4","x5","x6","x7","x8","x9")]
dat = as.data.frame( lapply(tmp, cut, 2, labels=FALSE) ) - 1

model = ' trait =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 '
fit = cfa(model, data=dat, ordered=names(dat), std.lv=TRUE) 

# Thresholds computed by lavaan
inspect(fit,"coef")$tau

# Now using glm...
coef( glm(x1 ~ 1, dat, family=binomial(link="probit")) )
coef( glm(x2 ~ 1, dat, family=binomial(link="probit")) )
coef( glm(x3 ~ 1, dat, family=binomial(link="probit")) )

# etc..

Thanks,  Mike

messages.author: b41ff7fc7cd0f193
messages.subject: Re: Direction of trait scale
parts:
I think lavaan takes the first response level as item endorsement. If responses are coded 0:1 then 0 is "success".  

p = prop.table(table(dat$x1))    # Response probability
qnorm(p[1])                            # Threshold for success 0 
qnorm(p[2])                            #  1 - threshold

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Direction of trait scale
parts: When I compute binary indicator thresholds using glm they have the opposite sign to thresholds computed by lavaan.

glm() does not estimate a threshold, it estimates the intercept.  Because your glm() model has not predictors, it's intercept is the grand "mean", or the z score corresponding to an overall probability that x1 == 1.
Is the scale direction arbitrary or is there some reason why these signs are opposite?

For binary data, threshold == -1 * intercept (similar sign-switching equality for more ordered categories).  If you override the defaults, you can estimate intercepts instead of thresholds for your latent item responses.

tau0.nuFree <- c(' trait =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 ',
                 paste0("x", 1:9, " | 0*t1"),
                 paste0("x", 1:9, " ~ NA*1"))
out <- cfa(tau0.nuFree, data=dat, ordered=names(dat), std.lv=TRUE)
summary(out)

Notice the intercepts match your glm() output.  So yes, it is in a sense arbitrary whether you fix thresholds and estimate intercepts or vice versa, because the parameterizations lead to equivalent implications (model-implied probabilities and tetrachoric correlations).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics

messages.author: b41ff7fc7cd0f193
messages.subject: Re: Direction of trait scale
parts:
Hi,

yes the intercepts are fixed by default. I now see the scale direction makes sense if we come from polytomous indicators with ordered levels.

dat = as.data.frame( lapply(tmp, cut, 4, labels=FALSE) ) - 1     # 4 levels

# Thresholds for item x1
p = prop.table(table(dat$x1))
qnorm(cumsum(p))                 # First three elements are thresholds along scale


thanks, Mike
